test_cases.title: Valid login establishes session cookie
test_cases.objective: Verify POST /api/v1/auth/login with valid seeded credentials returns 200, sets a sessionid cookie with HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax (Secure outside local), and /auth/me then returns the user identity, role, and scopes.
test_cases.preconditions: Compose stack up; migrations + seed applied; user 'operator' exists with documented dev password.
test_cases.test_data: operator / dev password from README (local seed)
steps: GET /api/v1/auth/csrf to obtain csrftoken cookie
POST /api/v1/auth/login with X-CSRFToken header and JSON {username, password}
Inspect Set-Cookie attributes on sessionid
GET /api/v1/auth/me with session cookie
test_cases.expected_result: 200 on login; sessionid cookie HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure when not on localhost; /auth/me returns 200 with display name, role='operator', scopes, and capability flags; response JSON only (no stack traces).

test_cases.title: Invalid login gives generic failure without user enumeration
test_cases.objective: Verify wrong password and non-existent username produce identical generic error responses (same status, same message, similar timing class) and no indication which part failed.
steps: POST /auth/login with valid username + wrong password; record status/body
POST /auth/login with non-existent username; record status/body
Compare response bodies and codes
test_cases.expected_result: Both return 401 with the error envelope, identical generic message, code AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED or equivalent; no field_errors revealing username validity; no session cookie set.

test_cases.title: Logout invalidates session
test_cases.objective: Verify POST /auth/logout ends the session server-side; subsequent /auth/me with the old cookie returns 401.
steps: Login; confirm /auth/me 200
POST /auth/logout with CSRF header
GET /auth/me again with same cookie jar
test_cases.expected_result: Logout returns 200/204; /auth/me afterwards returns 401 with AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED envelope.

test_cases.title: /auth/me exposes role, scopes, capability flags for permission-driven UI
test_cases.objective: Verify /auth/me payload contains role, organizational scopes, and capability flags sufficient for the frontend to hide unauthorized actions (design §14 rule 7).
test_cases.preconditions: Seeded users for each role exist.
test_cases.test_data: admin, manager, deptmgr, operator, employee, auditor
steps: Login as each seeded role user
GET /auth/me and compare role/scopes/capabilities across roles
test_cases.expected_result: Each role returns distinct, correct capabilities (e.g. employee lacks asset:create; auditor lacks all mutations; admin unrestricted); scopes list present for scoped roles.

test_cases.title: Unauthenticated access to protected endpoints returns 401 envelope
test_cases.objective: Verify GET /api/v1/assets, /dashboard/summary, /saved-views without a session return 401 with the standard error envelope and no data.
steps: GET each protected endpoint without cookies
Validate response body against error-envelope schema {error:{code,message,field_errors,correlation_id,retryable}}
test_cases.expected_result: All return 401 with code AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED, valid envelope, correlation_id present, no resource data leaked.

test_cases.title: Session identifier rotates on login
test_cases.objective: Verify the session ID value changes at login (session fixation mitigation) while preserving the session.
steps: Obtain an anonymous/pre-login sessionid value (if any) or note cookie state
POST /auth/login
Compare sessionid value before/after login
test_cases.expected_result: Session key rotates on successful login; old session key is invalid afterwards.

test_cases.title: CSRF enforced on unsafe methods
test_cases.objective: Verify POST/PATCH/DELETE requests with a valid session but missing/invalid CSRF token are rejected.
steps: POST /api/v1/assets with session cookie but no X-CSRFToken header
POST /auth/logout with no CSRF header
Repeat with an invalid token value
test_cases.expected_result: Requests rejected (403 per Django CSRF behavior) with no state change; same requests with valid token succeed.

test_cases.title: Login endpoint is rate limited
test_cases.objective: Verify repeated failed login attempts trigger rate limiting/backoff per design §13 (429 RATE_LIMITED or documented lockout).
test_cases.preconditions: Stack up; test uses a throwaway account to avoid locking seeded users.
test_cases.test_data: employee credentials with wrong password, N attempts (N per documented policy, default try 10-15)
steps: POST /auth/login with bad credentials repeatedly until limit
Observe status codes and envelope
test_cases.expected_result: After threshold, responses are 429 with code RATE_LIMITED and retryable indicator or documented lockout behavior; generic message retained (no enumeration).

test_cases.title: Expired/invalid session redirects to sign-in with return URL (UI)
test_cases.objective: Verify the SPA redirects to /login?next=... on 401 and, after re-auth, lands on the originally requested deep link (design §12 session-expiry UX).
test_cases.preconditions: App running; a known asset detail URL exists.
steps: Without a session, navigate to /assets/<uuid>
Observe redirect to /login with next param
Sign in as operator
Verify landing on the original asset detail page
test_cases.expected_result: Redirect occurs with encoded next URL; post-login navigation lands on the deep link; no private data rendered before auth.

test_cases.title: Login success/failure/logout produce audit events
test_cases.objective: Verify successful login, failed login, and logout each create AuditEvent rows with actor (or attempted identifier), action, timestamp UTC, outcome, and correlation ID.
test_cases.preconditions: Admin access to audit query or DB inspection available in test env.
steps: Perform failed login, successful login, logout
Query AuditEvent records (admin API or DB) for the three actions
test_cases.expected_result: Three audit rows exist with correct action types, outcomes (failure/success), UTC timestamps, and correlation IDs; failed attempt does not record the password.

test_cases.title: Local auth cannot be enabled in production settings
test_cases.objective: Verify that with APP_ENV=production and LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED unset, the app fails fast or hard-disables local login; with explicit LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED=true a loud warning/override path per design is required.
test_cases.preconditions: Ability to run Django check/startup with production settings in test harness.
steps: Run backend startup/check with production settings and no LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED
Repeat with LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED=true and observe logged warning/behavior
test_cases.expected_result: Startup refuses or disables local auth in production by default; override requires explicit env and logs a prominent warning.

test_cases.title: Non-admin roles cannot write reference data
test_cases.objective: Verify POST/PATCH on /api/v1/reference-data/* by operator/employee/auditor is denied, while admin succeeds.
test_cases.preconditions: Seeded users per role; valid CSRF.
steps: As operator: POST /reference-data/categories
As employee and auditor: repeat
As admin: repeat and then clean up
test_cases.expected_result: Operator/employee/auditor receive 403 PERMISSION_DENIED envelope; admin receives 201; denials leak no data.

test_cases.title: Asset list is filtered by organizational scope
test_cases.objective: Verify a department-scoped user (deptmgr/employee) sees only assets within their scopes in GET /assets, while admin/asset_manager see all permitted records.
test_cases.preconditions: Seed includes assets across multiple departments/locations; deptmgr scoped to one department.
steps: As admin: GET /assets, record count
As deptmgr: GET /assets, record count and department values of results
Cross-check that no out-of-scope asset appears for deptmgr
test_cases.expected_result: deptmgr count < admin count; every returned asset is within deptmgr scope; envelope pagination correct on both.

test_cases.title: Direct detail access to out-of-scope asset returns 404 (no existence leak)
test_cases.objective: Verify a scoped user requesting GET /assets/{uuid} for an out-of-scope asset receives 404 (not 403), avoiding existence disclosure per design §11.2.
test_cases.preconditions: Known UUID of an asset outside deptmgr's scope.
test_cases.test_data: out-of-scope asset UUID from admin listing
steps: As admin, identify an asset outside deptmgr scope
As deptmgr, GET /assets/{that uuid}
Also GET a random non-existent UUID and compare responses
test_cases.expected_result: Both requests return indistinguishable 404 NOT_FOUND envelopes; no difference in body that reveals existence.

test_cases.title: Financial fields hidden from roles without finance.view
test_cases.objective: Verify purchase_price/purchase_currency and other financial fields are absent from asset serializers for roles lacking finance.view, and present (as money object) for authorized roles.
test_cases.preconditions: Seeded asset with purchase price exists.
steps: As employee: GET /assets/{uuid} and list response fields
As admin/asset_manager (whichever holds finance.view): same request
Verify money object shape {amount, currency} where present
test_cases.expected_result: Financial fields absent (not null-masked) for unauthorized roles; authorized roles receive {"amount": "1234.56", "currency": "USD"} decimal-string format; never a float.

test_cases.title: Employee cannot create assets (vertical privilege check)
test_cases.objective: Verify POST /assets as employee returns 403 and creates nothing.
steps: As employee, POST /api/v1/assets with a fully valid payload
Verify response and that asset count is unchanged
test_cases.expected_result: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED envelope; no Asset, LifecycleEvent, or AuditEvent-created record for the attempted asset.

test_cases.title: Auditor role is read-only across all endpoints
test_cases.objective: Verify auditor can GET permitted resources but every mutation (POST/PATCH/DELETE) is denied.
test_cases.test_data: asset PATCH payload; saved-view POST payload
steps: As auditor: GET /assets (expect 200)
PATCH /assets/{uuid}; POST /saved-views; POST /assets — expect denials
test_cases.expected_result: Reads succeed within scope; all mutations return 403 PERMISSION_DENIED; no state changes.

test_cases.title: Horizontal escalation: user cannot act on another user's saved views
test_cases.objective: Verify PATCH/DELETE on a saved view owned by a different user is denied/404 even for same-role users.
test_cases.preconditions: Two operator-level users (or operator + manager) each with an own saved view.
test_cases.test_data: saved view UUID owned by manager
steps: As operator, PATCH and DELETE manager's saved view UUID
Verify manager's view is unchanged
test_cases.expected_result: Requests denied (403 or 404); target view unchanged; denial audited if policy requires.

test_cases.title: UI hides unauthorized actions and gates not-yet-delivered modules
test_cases.objective: Verify the frontend hides create/edit/admin actions for roles lacking capabilities, and Cycle 2/3 modules (Scan/Tasks/Imports etc.) are either absent, marked 'coming soon', or permission-gated; backend remains the enforcement boundary.
test_cases.preconditions: App running; sessions for employee and operator.
steps: As employee: verify no 'New asset' affordance, no edit buttons on detail
Attempt direct navigation to /assets/new as employee
Check Scan/Tasks bottom-nav entries show accessible 'coming soon' empty states or are hidden
test_cases.expected_result: Unauthorized UI actions hidden; direct URL access to /assets/new as employee results in 403 page or redirect; stubs are accessible-but-inert with proper labeling; server still rejects forged API calls (covered by TC-FR-002-05).

test_cases.title: Create asset with valid required fields succeeds atomically
test_cases.objective: Verify POST /assets with all category-driven required fields returns 201, the asset is retrievable, and Asset + initial LifecycleEvent + AuditEvent are created atomically.
test_cases.preconditions: Operator session; category with attribute definitions seeded; valid CSRF.
test_cases.test_data: {tag, name, category, status, condition, department, location, serial_number}
steps: POST /api/v1/assets with valid payload
GET the returned asset by UUID
Verify one initial LifecycleEvent and one AuditEvent exist for the asset
test_cases.expected_result: 201 with asset representation (UUID, version=1); detail GET 200; exactly one 'created/registered' lifecycle event and one audit event with before=null/after snapshot, actor=operator, correlation ID echoed.

test_cases.title: Missing/invalid required fields return 400 with per-field errors
test_cases.objective: Verify validation failures return the error envelope with field_errors keyed per field and user-safe messages.
test_cases.test_data: payload missing name/category; invalid date format; invalid reference UUIDs
steps: POST /assets with {} empty body
POST with invalid category UUID and malformed purchase_date
Inspect field_errors keys
test_cases.expected_result: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED; field_errors lists each offending field with a message; nothing persisted; envelope has correlation_id and retryable=false.

test_cases.title: Duplicate asset tag rejected
test_cases.objective: Verify creating an asset with an existing tag fails with DUPLICATE_TAG (400 or 409 per API mapping) and tag uniqueness holds for all time including archived records.
steps: POST /assets with tag T
Confirm DB-level uniqueness by attempting direct second create via API again
test_cases.expected_result: Request rejected with code DUPLICATE_TAG; no second asset created; error message is user-safe.

test_cases.title: Duplicate pre-check returns non-blocking warnings
test_cases.objective: Verify POST /assets/{id}/check-duplicates (or pre-check endpoint) flags possible duplicates by serial number and manufacturer+model as warnings without blocking save.
test_cases.preconditions: Existing asset with serial S, manufacturer M, model Mo.
test_cases.test_data: candidate payload reusing serial S; another reusing M+Mo
steps: Call check-duplicates with serial S
Call with same manufacturer+model, different serial
Proceed to save despite warnings
test_cases.expected_result: Responses include structured warnings listing matched assets/fields; HTTP 200 (non-blocking); save with warnings succeeds (unless category enforces serial uniqueness — then documented 400/409).

test_cases.title: Server-generated tags are unique under concurrent creation
test_cases.objective: Verify the AssetTagSequence-based tag generation produces unique tags when multiple creates occur concurrently (locked increments).
test_cases.preconditions: Server-side tag generation enabled; operator session.
test_cases.test_data: 10 concurrent create requests without client-supplied tags
steps: Fire 10 parallel POST /assets requests (pytest threads or async client)
Collect returned tags
test_cases.expected_result: All 10 succeed with distinct, sequence-conformant tags; no DUPLICATE_TAG errors; no gaps indicating lost updates.

test_cases.title: Draft save permitted with incomplete optional data
test_cases.objective: Verify an asset can be saved in Draft status with minimal identity fields, per FR-003 draft-save allowance.
test_cases.preconditions: Draft status exists in seeded statuses.
steps: POST /assets with draft payload omitting optional fields
GET asset and confirm status
test_cases.expected_result: 201; asset persisted with Draft status; required-field rules for Draft are the documented minimal set.

test_cases.title: Idempotency-Key prevents duplicate creates on retry
test_cases.objective: Verify repeating POST /assets with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original response without creating a second asset (24h TTL, scoped per user+endpoint).
steps: POST /assets with key K; record response and asset UUID
Repeat identical request with key K
Repeat with same key but different payload (expect conflict or documented behavior)
Count assets created
test_cases.expected_result: Exactly one asset created; second identical request returns the stored response (same UUID); same key + different payload rejected per documented behavior.

test_cases.title: Category attribute values validated against definitions
test_cases.objective: Verify category_attributes JSON is validated against CategoryAttributeDefinition (type, required, choice options) and invalid values are rejected with field errors.
test_cases.preconditions: Seeded category with attribute definitions incl. a required choice attribute.
test_cases.test_data: attributes with wrong type (string for number), missing required key, invalid choice
steps: POST /assets with each invalid attribute variant
POST with fully valid attributes
test_cases.expected_result: Invalid variants → 400 with attribute-specific field_errors; valid variant → 201 and attributes round-trip on GET.

test_cases.title: XSS payloads in text fields are stored inertly and escaped in UI
test_cases.objective: Verify script/HTML payloads in name/description are accepted as data (or rejected per policy) but never executed: API returns them as plain text and the UI renders escaped content.
test_cases.preconditions: Operator session; browser for UI verification.
steps: Create asset with XSS payloads
Open asset list and detail in browser; confirm no script execution (no alert, no injected nodes)
Verify API returns raw string (not sanitized into corruption) and CSP header present
test_cases.expected_result: No script execution anywhere; values display as literal text; CSP header present on frontend responses.

test_cases.title: Asset detail returns complete identity representation
test_cases.objective: Verify GET /assets/{uuid} returns identity fields (tag, name, category, status, condition, department, location, custodian, serial, manufacturer/model, version, timestamps) per data model.
steps: GET /assets/{uuid} as operator
Validate fields against OpenAPI schema
test_cases.expected_result: 200 with all identity fields; UUID (not bigint) exposed; version integer present; datetimes ISO 8601 with TZ.

test_cases.title: Edit asset succeeds and increments version
test_cases.objective: Verify PATCH /assets/{uuid} with correct version (body or If-Match) applies changes, increments version, and updates updated_at.
test_cases.preconditions: Operator session; asset at version v.
steps: GET asset, note version v and updated_at
PATCH with version v
GET again
test_cases.expected_result: 200; name updated; version = v+1; updated_at advanced; response carries new version for subsequent edits.

test_cases.title: Stale version update rejected with 409 VERSION_CONFLICT
test_cases.objective: Verify a PATCH carrying an outdated version fails with 409 VERSION_CONFLICT and no partial update occurs; UI surfaces a conflict prompt.
test_cases.preconditions: Asset at version v; two sessions (or sequential requests).
test_cases.test_data: two PATCHes both with version v
steps: PATCH #1 with version v (succeeds, now v+1)
PATCH #2 with stale version v
Verify only PATCH #1's changes persisted
E2E: open edit form in two tabs, save both, verify second shows conflict message with reload path
test_cases.expected_result: Second PATCH → 409 VERSION_CONFLICT envelope; stored data equals PATCH #1 only; UI displays a clear conflict state (no silent overwrite).

test_cases.title: Asset history endpoint returns chronological lifecycle events
test_cases.objective: Verify GET /assets/{uuid}/history returns the asset's lifecycle events in reverse-chronological order with actor, timestamp, type, and summary.
test_cases.preconditions: Asset with create + at least one update event.
steps: GET /assets/{uuid}/history
Verify ordering, event fields, and pagination if applicable
test_cases.expected_result: Events ordered newest-first; each has type, actor, occurred_at (UTC, TZ-aware), summary; cycle-1 scope covers lifecycle+audit-level events.

test_cases.title: Material updates audited with before/after snapshots
test_cases.objective: Verify each asset update writes an AuditEvent containing before and after JSON for changed fields, actor, UTC timestamp, and correlation ID.
test_cases.preconditions: Asset updated via PATCH; audit readable in test env.
steps: PATCH asset fields
Inspect the resulting AuditEvent row
test_cases.expected_result: AuditEvent exists with action=update, before/after containing the changed fields' old/new values, actor identity, correlation_id matching the API request, outcome=success.

test_cases.title: Invalid or non-existent asset UUID returns 404 envelope
test_cases.objective: Verify GET/PATCH on a random UUID or malformed identifier returns a clean 404 (or 400 for malformed) envelope, never a 500 or stack trace.
steps: GET /assets/<random-uuid>
GET /assets/not-a-uuid
test_cases.expected_result: 404 NOT_FOUND for valid-but-missing UUID; 400 or 404 for malformed id per documented behavior; both use the error envelope; no internals leaked.

test_cases.title: Edit form: unsaved-changes guard and error-summary focus management
test_cases.objective: Verify navigating away from a dirty edit form prompts a confirmation; failed submit moves focus to an error summary with per-field errors and preserves entered values.
test_cases.preconditions: Edit page for a seeded asset.
test_cases.test_data: modify name; submit a form with a deliberately invalid field
steps: Change a field, attempt browser/router navigation away — expect guard prompt
Submit form with an invalid value — expect error summary receives focus, fields keep values, per-field errors associated with inputs
test_cases.expected_result: Guard prompt appears and blocks navigation until confirmed; error summary focused on failed submit; aria-describedby links errors to fields; no data loss.

test_cases.title: Global search ranks exact tag match first
test_cases.objective: Verify GET /search/assets?q=<exact tag> returns the exact-tag asset as the first result, ahead of partial matches.
test_cases.preconditions: Seeded assets with known tags incl. one whose tag is a substring of another's name.
steps: GET /search/assets?q=<tag>
Inspect ordering and match metadata
test_cases.expected_result: Exact tag match is result #1; results scoped to caller's permissions; response time reasonable (<2s p95 target, smoke-level check).

test_cases.title: Search matches serial, name, model, custodian, location
test_cases.objective: Verify search finds assets by serial number, name substring, model, custodian name, and location name per FR-005.
test_cases.preconditions: Seeded assets with distinct values in each searchable field.
test_cases.test_data: known serial, name fragment, model, custodian, location
steps: Run one search per field type
Verify expected asset appears in results
test_cases.expected_result: Each field type yields its matching asset; no crashes on special characters (%, _, quotes) in q.

test_cases.title: List filters by status, category, department, location, condition
test_cases.objective: Verify GET /assets supports the documented filter parameters and combinations, returning only matching in-scope assets.
steps: Apply each filter singly and verify every result matches
Apply combined filters and verify intersection semantics
Apply invalid filter value — expect 400 or empty result per contract
test_cases.expected_result: All returned rows satisfy all active filters; invalid filter values handled per documented contract (no 500).

test_cases.title: Server-side sorting on supported columns
test_cases.objective: Verify ?ordering= and ?ordering=- on documented sortable fields (name, tag, updated_at, status) return correctly ordered results.
steps: Request each ordering and verify result sequence
Request an unsupported ordering field
test_cases.expected_result: Ascending/descending orders correct; unsupported field rejected (400) or ignored per documented contract — never 500.

test_cases.title: Pagination envelope and page_size limits enforced
test_cases.objective: Verify list responses use {count, next, previous, results}; default page_size=25; page_size>100 clamped or rejected; page navigation consistent.
steps: GET /assets default — verify envelope and 25 items
GET with page_size=10 and page=2 — verify correct slice and next/previous links
GET page_size=500 — verify max-100 handling
GET out-of-range page — verify documented behavior (404 or empty)
test_cases.expected_result: Envelope always present; defaults and max enforced per D-09; no duplicate/skipped rows across consecutive pages.

test_cases.title: Filter/sort/pagination state synchronized to URL query params
test_cases.objective: Verify the asset register reflects filters, sort, and page in the URL; reloading or sharing the URL restores the identical view (bookmarkable).
test_cases.test_data: apply status filter + sort by name + page 2
steps: Apply filters/sort/page in UI; observe URL
Copy URL, open in fresh browser context, sign in, verify identical view
Use browser back/forward and verify state restoration
test_cases.expected_result: URL contains all state; fresh load reproduces identical results and active-filter chips; history navigation works.

test_cases.title: Search results respect organizational scope
test_cases.objective: Verify search never returns out-of-scope assets to scoped users even when the query exactly matches an out-of-scope tag.
test_cases.preconditions: Out-of-scope asset with known tag (relative to deptmgr).
steps: As deptmgr, search for the out-of-scope tag
Verify result set
test_cases.expected_result: Out-of-scope asset absent from results; response indistinguishable from 'no matches'.

test_cases.title: Empty search/filter results show a proper empty state
test_cases.objective: Verify a query/filter combination with no matches renders an accessible empty state with guidance (not a blank table or error).
steps: Search for a nonsense string; apply impossible filter combo
Inspect empty-state region
test_cases.expected_result: Empty state displayed with clear text and a reset/clear-filters action; announced via live region or reachable by screen reader; table headers/structure remain coherent.

test_cases.title: Create, apply, and delete own saved view
test_cases.objective: Verify POST /saved-views stores a filter configuration, GET lists own views, applying it reproduces the filter state, and DELETE removes it.
steps: POST /saved-views; GET /saved-views and confirm presence
In UI, apply the view and verify filters/URL update accordingly
DELETE the view; confirm 404 afterwards
test_cases.expected_result: Full CRUD round-trip works for own views; applying the view restores exact filter state; deleted view gone from list and direct GET.

test_cases.title: Other users' private saved views are invisible and immutable
test_cases.objective: Verify private saved views of another user do not appear in listings and cannot be read/modified/deleted directly.
test_cases.preconditions: View owned by manager; operator session.
steps: As operator: GET /saved-views (verify absence), GET/PATCH/DELETE the UUID directly
test_cases.expected_result: View absent from operator's list; direct access returns 404 (or 403 per contract) with no state change.

test_cases.title: Default view selection persists per user
test_cases.objective: Verify marking a saved view as default makes the asset register load with that view applied for that user only.
steps: Mark view A default via API/UI
Reload /assets and verify view A applied
Log in as different user and verify their register is unaffected
test_cases.expected_result: Default applied on register load for the owning user only; setting a new default unsets the previous one.

test_cases.title: Dashboard summary returns scope-correct counts
test_cases.objective: Verify GET /dashboard/summary returns basic KPI counts (totals, by status/category as delivered) computed only over the caller's permitted record set.
steps: GET /dashboard/summary as admin and as deptmgr
Independently compute deptmgr-visible counts via filtered /assets queries
Compare totals
test_cases.expected_result: deptmgr totals equal the independently computed in-scope counts; admin sees org-wide totals; no cross-scope leakage; response shape per OpenAPI.

test_cases.title: Dashboard KPI cards render loading, empty, and error states
test_cases.objective: Verify the dashboard shows skeletons while loading, a coherent empty state when counts are zero, and an error state with correlation ID on API failure.
test_cases.preconditions: App running; ability to simulate failure (e.g. stop backend or use a route mock in Playwright).
steps: Load dashboard; observe skeleton then KPI cards
Intercept /dashboard/summary to return 500 envelope; reload
Verify error UI shows user-safe message + correlation ID, with retry
test_cases.expected_result: All three states implemented accessibly; no raw exception text; retry re-fetches.

test_cases.title: KPI indicators link to correctly filtered lists
test_cases.objective: Verify clicking a KPI (e.g. by-status count) navigates to /assets with the corresponding filter applied and the list count reconciles with the KPI.
test_cases.preconditions: Dashboard with at least one drill-through KPI as delivered in Cycle 1.
steps: Click a KPI card link
Verify destination URL filters and that list count equals the KPI number
test_cases.expected_result: Navigation applies matching filters; KPI and list totals reconcile for the user's scope.

test_cases.title: Asset mutations create AuditEvents with correlation IDs
test_cases.objective: Verify create/update operations write AuditEvent rows whose correlation_id matches the request's X-Correlation-ID and whose actor/action/target/timestamp fields are complete.
test_cases.preconditions: Audit readable in test env (admin API or DB).
steps: Send create and update requests with known correlation IDs
Fetch corresponding AuditEvents and compare
test_cases.expected_result: Audit rows found by correlation ID; actor=user identity, target=asset UUID, action correct, created_at UTC, outcome recorded.

test_cases.title: Audit hash chain is intact and tamper-evident
test_cases.objective: Verify AuditEvent rows chain via prev_hash/record_hash (SHA-256) and that recomputation over a sequence validates; tampering (simulated in a throwaway test DB) breaks verification.
test_cases.preconditions: Several audit events exist; test harness can recompute hashes.
steps: Recompute record_hash for a sequence of events using documented canonicalization
Verify each prev_hash equals prior record_hash
In a disposable test DB, modify one row's payload and re-run verification
test_cases.expected_result: Chain verifies on unmodified data; verification fails after tampering.

test_cases.title: Audit events are append-only via application surface
test_cases.objective: Verify no API endpoint permits updating or deleting audit events, and app DB role lacks UPDATE/DELETE on the audit table where enforced.
test_cases.test_data: attempt PATCH/DELETE on audit resource paths
steps: Attempt PATCH/DELETE against any audit endpoint (expect method not allowed / 404 / 405)
Where DB permissions are enforced, attempt direct UPDATE as app role in test DB
test_cases.expected_result: No application path mutates audit history; attempts are denied and, where policy requires, logged.

test_cases.title: Reference data readable by authenticated users
test_cases.objective: Verify GET endpoints for categories, statuses, conditions, departments, locations, cost-centers, suppliers return seeded data to any authenticated role and 401 to anonymous callers.
steps: As employee, GET each collection
Anonymously, GET each collection
test_cases.expected_result: Authenticated reads return 200 with seeded rows (13 statuses, 6 conditions, 5 categories, etc. per §10.4); anonymous → 401 envelope.

test_cases.title: Admin reference-data writes are audited
test_cases.objective: Verify admin create/update of a reference-data record succeeds and writes an AuditEvent with before/after.
steps: POST /reference-data/suppliers as admin
PATCH the created record
Verify audit events for both operations
test_cases.expected_result: 201/200 responses; two AuditEvents with correct actor, target, and before/after; unique code constraint enforced on duplicates.

test_cases.title: Error envelope shape consistent across 400/401/403/404/409

test_cases.title: Correlation IDs generated and echoed end-to-end
